name: isMFAEnabled
definition: CONTESTED -- no single meaning is held in production. Eight integrations answer this key with five incompatible meanings, listed under conflict.positions; until the owner rules, no new implementation may be added under this name.
population: unknown -- differs per position: a policy object, a tenant method catalogue, the set of sign-on rules, the set of accounts, or the customer's own application end users
evidenceRequiredForTrue: unknown -- the five positions require five different reads; see conflict.positions

conflict.summary: All eight integrations agree on the TYPE (boolean) and disagree on what true asserts. Five meanings: a policy or setting exists; a method is available and something demands it; at least one sign-on path requires a second factor; every account has MFA; the customer's own application end users have MFA. It is dormant only because the six requirements asking it name 'Multifactor Authentication' while every answering integration is filed elsewhere -- repair the taxonomy (Wave F) first and all five meanings switch on at once under one name.

positions.meaning: A policy or setting object says MFA is on: Okta's MFA_ENROLL policy has status active; Ping Federate has at least one MFA-type IdP adapter configured; Saviynt's security settings report MFA enabled.
positions.source: Okta: plan D1 -- the undeletable system MFA_ENROLL Default Policy every org has, so true for an org with no MFA (86ded564/mfa_transform.py:103-110). Ping and Saviynt: RTA descriptions only (defs snapshot), code not read -- V0.

positions.meaning: MFA methods are enabled at the tenant AND at least one enabled Conditional Access policy's grantControls.builtInControls contains mfa.
positions.population: tenant method catalogue plus the Conditional Access policy set
positions.source: iam-mfa.md F-iam-mfa-18: is_enabled = methods_available and mfa_enforced (:120-121). The RTA description says only 'methods are enabled', which understates the code.

positions.meaning: At least one sign-on-allowing rule across the global session and authentication policies requires two factors.
positions.source: iam-mfa.md F-iam-mfa-03 (replayed on a real body): the same file emits isMFAEnforcedForUsers with the stricter 'every rule' meaning (:26-28, :66, :214-215). Correct as written; do not 'fix' the shared URL.

positions.meaning: Every enabled account (operator, system user) has a second factor enrolled.
positions.source: key-registry.md F-KEY-13 (RTA descriptions; code cross-checked only for Okta). Acre also emits mfaCoveragePercentage.

positions.meaning: Every Supabase project verifies a second factor for ITS END USERS -- the customer's own application users, not the customer's workforce.
positions.population: the customer's application end users, per project
positions.source: key-registry.md F-KEY-13; RTA description. Also emits mfaCoveragePercentage -- over PROJECTS, a third population under that name.

proposedResolution.summary: Retire isMFAEnabled as a name with no independent meaning and move each position to a key that says what it measures. Two reviewers disagreed on the destination for the middle positions and both are recorded: key-registry F-KEY-13 deprecates isMFAEnabled entirely (enforcement vendors to isMFAEnforcedForUsers, policy-only vendors to isMFAPolicyConfigured); iam-mfa F-iam-mfa-18 calls Azure's 'available AND demanded' the right definition of isMFAEnabled itself. This proposal follows F-KEY-13 because Azure's definition is still 'at least one policy', which isMFAEnforcedForUsers (every path, 49 requirements) is not.

splitKeys.name: isMFAPolicyConfigured
splitKeys.definition: An MFA policy, adapter or setting is configured; nothing about whether any sign-on path requires it was read. Presence evidence, weaker than enforcement.

splitKeys.name: isMFARequiredByAnyPolicy
splitKeys.definition: At least one enabled access policy or rule that can grant sign-on requires a second factor.

splitKeys.name: isMFAEnforcedForUsers
splitKeys.definition: Every authentication path that grants a user access requires a second factor; no path accepts a single factor.
wouldTake: none of today's isMFAEnabled answers -- listed so nobody aliases isMFAEnabled onto it

splitKeys.name: mfaCoveragePercentage
splitKeys.definition: Percentage of enabled workforce accounts with a second factor enrolled.

splitKeys.name: isAppEndUserMFAEnforced
splitKeys.definition: Every project of the customer's own application requires its end users to verify a second factor.

decision.question: Do we retire isMFAEnabled into the five keys proposed (F-KEY-13), or keep it with Azure's 'methods available AND at least one policy requires MFA' as its single meaning (F-iam-mfa-18) and move only the policy-presence and population-mismatch vendors off it? Either way this must be decided before Wave F repairs the MFA category.
